title: Simultaneous clopen lisse trivialization and complete restriction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and put $R_{n,T}=(R/\varpi^n)_T$ and $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R_{n,T}$, using constant sheaves and inverse limits [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Use the unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_T))$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A complex $M$ is quotient-tower complete if its canonical quotient maps exhibit it as $R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})$, with the quotient transitions and with the terms restricted to $B_T$-scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Assume that $T$ is affine and evaluation at $T$ sends every epimorphism of sheaves of sets to a surjection. Let $J$ be a finite set and, for each $j\in J$, let $F_j$ be a locally constant sheaf of $k_T$-modules with finite-dimensional $k$-module local models [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. There is a finite partition $T=\coprod_i U_i$ by clopen subschemes, meaning open subschemes whose underlying subsets are closed [def-weil-open-immersion], such that $F_j|_{U_i}\cong k_{U_i}^{\oplus r_{ij}}$ for finite integers $r_{ij}\geq0$. Each $U_i$ is quasi-compact and evaluation on $U_i$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. For every sheaf $C$ of commutative rings on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$, evaluation $\Gamma(U_i,-)$ on $C$-module sheaves is exact, and $C^{\oplus r}$ is a projective object for every finite $r$: maps from it lift along epimorphisms. Moreover $B_T|_{U_i}\cong B_{U_i}$ canonically. Ordinary restriction to $U_i$ preserves quotient-tower completeness and commutes with derived reductions, with the canonical quotient projections and their reduction transitions. If $M_1=M\otimes^L_{B_T}k_T$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ after restriction to every site object, then $(M|_{U_i})\otimes^L_{B_{U_i}}k_{U_i}$ has the same amplitude. Here Tor amplitude means vanishing of $H^q(-\otimes^L_{k_V}L)$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, for every site object $V$ and every degree-zero $k_V$-module sheaf $L$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The empty partition is allowed for $T=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, finite disjoint open decomposition in the base case and restriction of the local models. The covering argument is Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, expanded from categorical weak contractibility; exact evaluation is Tag 0946, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-w-contractible. Parent proof steps 2-3.

proof.text: For each $j$, take a trivializing covering from the definition of locally constant. Intersect the finitely many coverings by successive fibre products over $T$; the base-change and composition axioms for coverings give one common trivializing covering. On each member every $F_j$ is a constant finite-dimensional $k$-module sheaf. Apply the finite-affine-refinement clause of [sk-def-pe-site] to the affine target $T$: obtain a finite covering $\{V_\alpha\to T\}_{\alpha\in A}$ with all $V_\alpha$ affine, each mapping to one member of the common covering. Restrict the trivializations along these site arrows: by [lem-pe-constant-module-restriction-universes] a sheaf isomorphic to the localized constant module sheaf with model $M$ over a site object stays isomorphic to the localized constant module sheaf with the same model $M$ after restriction along any arrow $W\to U$; the constant coefficient rings are identified by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. If $J$ is empty use the identity covering of $T$.

source.place: Tags 098B/098D, finite affine refinement; Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, base-case finite disjoint trivialization

proof.text: Form $P=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}V_\alpha$ and $p:P\to T$. The finite-coproduct theorem puts $P$ in $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and identifies its represented sheaf with the sheaf coproduct of the $h_{V_\alpha}$. The map $h_P\to h_T$ is locally surjective: for a map $W\to T$, pull back the covering of step 1; on $W\times_TV_\alpha$ the map to $P$ gives the required lift of that section. It is therefore an epimorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]. By the hypothesis on evaluation at $T$, the identity in $h_T(T)$ lifts to $h_P(T)$. Subcanonicity and Yoneda identify this lift with a scheme map $s:T\to P$ satisfying $ps=1_T$. Put $U_\alpha=s^{-1}(V_\alpha)$. The coprojections have pairwise disjoint clopen images covering $P$, so the $U_\alpha$ are pairwise disjoint clopens covering $T$. The open-factorization lemma supplies $s_\alpha:U_\alpha\to V_\alpha$ with $(V_\alpha\to T)s_\alpha=(U_\alpha\to T)$. Since $s_\alpha$ is an arrow of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, pull back the trivializations of step 1 along it by [lem-pe-constant-module-restriction-universes] and choose a finite basis of each module model: $F_j|_{U_\alpha}\cong k_{U_\alpha}^{\oplus r_{\alpha j}}$. Discard empty pieces. Each remaining piece is quasi-compact since it is closed in the quasi-compact affine $T$. If $T$ is empty discard all pieces.

source.place: Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, section and inverse-image partition argument; categorical section obtained as in sites.tex Tag 090K, lemma-w-contractible

proof.text: Fix a resulting clopen $U$ and write $Z=T\setminus U$. For a sheaf of sets $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, define $\widetilde F(V)=F(V\times_TU)$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. This is a sheaf because pulling a covering back to $U$ gives a covering. If $F\to G$ is an epimorphism and $g\in\widetilde G(V)$, the local-surjectivity criterion gives a covering of $V\times_TU$ on which $g$ lifts; together with $V\times_TZ$ this is a covering of $V$. Over the latter piece both extended sheaves have the singleton value at the empty scheme, so there is a lift there too. Thus $\widetilde F\to\widetilde G$ is an epimorphism. Evaluation at $T$ is surjective on this map by hypothesis, and its map on sections is exactly $F(U)\to G(U)$. This proves the required evaluation property on $U$ using only the local-surjectivity criterion and localized-site definitions.

source.place: Tags 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves, and 00Y0/03EH, localization and relocalization; elementary clopen extension argument

proof.text: For any commutative ring sheaf $C$ on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact] using step 3: evaluation preserves homology and hence exact sequences of $C$-module sheaves. A $C$-linear map $C^{\oplus r}\to H$ is specified by the images of its $r$ global basis sections, i.e. by an element of $H(U)^r$; conversely these sections define the map by $C$-linear combinations on every object. For an epimorphism $G\to H$, exact evaluation lifts each of these finitely many sections to $G(U)$ and hence lifts the given map. This proves projectivity, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0946, lemma-w-contractible, part (1), followed by the finite-free basis argument

proof.text: For each $n$, localized restriction identifies $(R/\varpi^n)_T|_U$ with $(R/\varpi^n)_U$, by the isomorphism that fixes all constant sections. The sectionwise inverse-limit formula of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit] consequently gives $B_T|_U\cong B_U$: at an object $V\to U$ both sides are the compatible tuples of sections of $(R/\varpi^n)$ on $V$. This is an isomorphism of ring sheaves since all operations are componentwise. Its composite with the $n$th quotient projection is the restriction of $B_T\to R_{n,T}$, and it identifies the quotient transitions because each is induced by $R/\varpi^{n+1}\to R/\varpi^n$ and the constant-section comparisons are natural.

source.place: Tag 00Y0, localized restriction; sectionwise ring limits as in the coefficient construction used by proetale.tex Tag 09C3

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] and [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus] to the finite partition and to the arbitrary ring sheaf $B_T$. They give exact ordinary restriction $r_U$ and its termwise triangulated functor on unbounded derived categories, as well as the natural scalar-extension comparisons. With step 5 these read $r_U(M\otimes^L_{B_T}R_{n,T})\cong r_UM\otimes^L_{B_U}R_{n,U}$. For $n=1$ the same statement identifies the residue-field reduction. Naturality in coefficient maps identifies all quotient transition maps. Compatibility with the tensor unit identifies the canonical maps from $M$: the unit $B_T\to R_{n,T}$ restricts to $B_U\to R_{n,U}$, so tensoring it with the identity of $M$ gives precisely the corresponding local quotient projection. Forgetting the quotient-ring action simply keeps the same underlying complex and the action through this ring map; restriction therefore also commutes with the specified restriction of scalars. Only the arbitrary-ring clauses of the cited nodes are used; no invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact functors on unbounded derived categories; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS/06YU, K-flat tensor, as packaged by the cited finite-clopen calculus

proof.text: Under the derived equivalence $D(B_T)\simeq\prod_iD(B_{U_i})$ of [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], let $e_U$ insert a complex in the $U$ coordinate and zero elsewhere. The product-category Hom formula and the restriction/insertion identities give $\operatorname{Hom}(e_UA,K)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,r_UK)$. Hence, if $P=\prod_nK_n$, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,r_UP)=\operatorname{Hom}(e_UA,P)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(e_UA,K_n)=\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(A,r_UK_n)$, naturally in $A$. Thus $r_UP$ with the restricted projections is the required product in the local derived category. Apply the triangulated functor $r_U$ to the Roos triangle that witnesses quotient-tower completeness of $M$. The middle arrow is still $1-s$, since its $n$th projection is the restriction of $\mathrm{pr}_n-t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. By [def-weil-derived-limit] the resulting triangle exhibits $r_UM$ as a derived limit of the restricted tower, with the restricted canonical quotient projections. Step 6 identifies this tower, its transitions and augmentation with the quotient-reduction tower of $r_UM$. This proves preservation of completeness and commutation with derived limits in the specified Roos-triangle sense.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit; elementary product-universal-property argument under the cited clopen derived equivalence

proof.text: By step 6, the reduction of $M|_U$ is $M_1|_U$. Every object $V\to U$ of $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is also an object over $T$, and the localized-site equivalence and relocalization identify $(M_1|_U)|_V$ with $M_1|_V$, including its constant coefficient ring $k_V$. For every degree-zero $k_V$-module sheaf $L$, its tensor with this identified complex has the vanishing outside $[a,b]$ required by the original hypothesis for the object $V\to T$. This is exactly the local Tor-amplitude assertion, with the same bounds. The empty scheme has only the zero module category, so the empty partition and the assertions there are valid.

tool_uses.why: General finite-clopen equivalence for arbitrary ring sheaves, used only for exact ordinary restriction; the unit has no gluing statement.
General finite-clopen derived equivalence, insertion identities and natural derived scalar-extension comparison; used as categorical tools for the local models, without changing the unit route.
General evaluation/homology theorem under exactly the categorical epimorphism hypothesis; supplies exact evaluation in step 4.
Identifies the small site of each open with the slice and its constant coefficients; a site-localization tool, not a replacement route.
General epi/local-surjectivity criterion for sets, used to split the finite cover and to extend an epimorphism across a clopen complement.
Representability as actual sheaves, needed to turn the lifted identity into a scheme section.
Finite affine coproduct exists in the pro-etale site and represents the sheaf coproduct; needed to obtain one scheme section.
Universal property of an open subscheme, to restrict the scheme section to each selected covering member.

Restriction of a localized constant module sheaf along a site arrow keeps the same model; used in steps 1-2 to move the finite-dimensional local models to the affine refinement and to the clopen pieces; the unit has no such statement.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q03-94f9c7825 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item (8 steps, no new nodes; statement and stmt_deps identical to live, where the item is still unsplit; not in the dropped list; no repair note; no SGA) against Stacks 098F (l. 2781-2807, section sigma and Zariski partition) and the 09C3 base case (finite disjoint affine-open decomposition). I also read every cited statement.

Checks:
- Step 2: the finite-coproduct node (V_alpha affine so qcqs, I finite), the local-surjectivity epi criterion, subcanonicity and Yoneda give s with ps=1. The scheme-coproduct node gives disjoint clopen images, and the open factorization applies to s on U_alpha.
- Step 3: the clopen extension F~(V)=F(V x_T U) is correct; on the complement piece V x_T Z both sheaves take the value at the empty scheme, a singleton.
- Step 4: the evaluation-exact node applies with W=U terminal, and Hom(C^r,H)=H(U)^r.
- Step 5: the sectionwise ring inverse limit.
- Step 6: only the arbitrary-R paragraphs of lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing and lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus are used (ell-invertibility belongs only to the unused constant-coefficient clause). The scalar-extension comparison is natural in coefficient maps.
- Step 7: the Roos-triangle definition with the product presupposed; r_U preserves products through the equivalence, and pr_n r_U(1-s) = pr_n - r_U f_n pr_{n+1}.
- Step 8: relocalization plus a hypothesis quantified over all site objects and all k_V-modules L.
- Edge cases: empty T, empty J, rank 0, differing ranks, zero ring, ell not invertible all hold. No cycle in a 261-node closure.

Fault (C4), steps 1-2: restricting the constant module local models along site arrows was attributed to lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization. That node only identifies the constant ring sheaf (clause 2).
